name: Kitchen Assistance
objectiveText: Calandrath at Cenarion Hold needs a batch of 10 Smoked Desert Dumplings . Smoked Desert Dumplings  ( 10 )

comments.body: There is a trade goods vendor in front of the building near the horde FP. You can buy the spices there. You can cook at any of the flaming braziers located in the area.

on my AH right now, 1 dumpling is 1g 9s buyout

ten Soothing spices are also 14s. So you just get 1.56g for this quest whereas you can easily make 10g from selling these.

3000 exp is very little as well. screw this quest, no followup, not worth it.
Have to have cooking of 285 to get this quest.
Once you share the recipe with the quest lady, it will be in your cooking book.
You can cook on the braziers - like in IF.
50 reputation

I got 3000 XP and about 50 rep points with the Cenarion Circle as well (at lvl 59). I do recommend getting some extra for yourself. :) The drop rate for the sandworm meat seems to be only about 10-20%, so it does take a while.
replies:
level 56 - 3000exp, 1g70s & 75 rep with CC.

The drop rate wasn't that bad - you can pick up the "Securing the Supply Lines" quest from Windcaller Proudhorn (out the front of the inn) and do that at the same time. Might even be a good idea to pick up "Deadly Desert Venom" from Beetix Ficklespragg (inside inn upstairs) cuz the mobs she wants you to kill spawn in the same area as the sandworms.

comments.body:
Just some 1.9 (when I finally completed the quest) information:

There is an Ironforge-like brazier in the stronghold now, as well as a general goods vendor that you can buy and cook after you get the sand worm meat.

Getting the sand worm meat itself was the hardest part... *grr*
Do this quest at the same time as [quest=8280]. The worms you need to kill for that quest will drop all the meat you'll need for this quest.

To reiterate, she sells flint/tinder,

BUT if you walk out of the inn and turn left, you will see a "cooking fire" that you can cook in.

It really wasnt that hard, it took me about 30 minutes to get the sandworm meat, and my cooking was 291 and it brought me up to 301. The money was nice, too bad she couldnt include about 10 of these in the reward too, hehe :)
she sells flint and tinder as well as simple wood.. so just make your own fire.
replies: There are braziers all over the town, they all work as cooking fires.

"That recipe sure will come in handy" ... WHAT recipe?  I did the quest before this, now I'm supposed to deliver some dumplings, but none of the vendors seem to sell the recipe (of course, if it's a limited supply item the odds of me finding it with the zone packed atm are slim).  I was not given the recipe by the questgiver, and it sure doesn't seem to be laying on the ground anywhere that I've seen, so ... How in the heck do I get the recipe?
replies: You automatically learn the recipe when you steal it from the book. I was confused by this as well, but then I just looked in my list of known recipes and there it was. They really need to add some kind of notification, or if there is one, they need to make it stand out more.

Although it's not obvious, but when you turn in this quest, you glow exactly as if you have just learned a new recipe by reading it from an item. At that time the combat log (or quest log, can't remember which) says that you have learned a new recipe: Smoked Desert Dumplings. 

I'm not sure what else they can do other than to explicitly say something in the quest reward...

The quest does not appear in your quest log.

You need to find the dusty recipe book or something close in the twilight camp and take a page from it. It is a quest item, not a recipe.

THEN the innkeeper will let you complete the quest and you get a recipe put into your cooking recipe list.

THEN you can make 10 smoked desert dumplings to complete the quest.
It does say "You have learned to create a new item: Smoked Desert Dumplings" in the system spam.
